channel.title: Arctura Technologies — Insights
channel.description: Notes from Arctura Technologies Inc. on health data, on-device AI, privacy engineering, and building consumer software in Canada.

item.title: Linnea 3.0 is on the App Store. Here is who is asked before anything about your family leaves your account.
item.description: Linnea 3.0 adds family links, Family AI, a family plan and invitations. What each one sends, who is asked first, and the one case where an adult answers for a child.

item.title: Android's agents have three ways into an app, and one needs nothing from the app. Here is what a health app should say about each.
item.description: Android's agents get three ways into an app: declared functions, a remote server or the screen itself. What a health app should say about each, and what Linnea says.

item.title: Siri AI is opening to every app. "On your device" now has three meanings, and a health app should say which one it means.
item.description: Apple is opening Siri AI to every app, and iOS 27.2 lets you exclude apps from it. Three things "on your device" can mean, and which one Linnea means for each feature.

item.title: Photo food logging has a benchmark problem. Here is what Linnea's 22.4% is measured on, and what it is not.
item.description: Two October preprints show why a photo calorie number depends on the dataset and why correction is part of the job. We say what Linnea's 22.4% is measured on.

item.title: Canada's privacy regulators set out six principles for AI in health. Here is where each one lives inside a health app.
item.description: Canada's privacy regulators published a resolution on AI in health on 29 October. We map its six principles onto what Linnea does, and what it does not.

item.title: A family menu needs everyone's tastes. Here is exactly what Linnea 2.8 took out of end-to-end encryption.
item.description: Linnea 2.8 adds a shared grocery list and a family menu. Privacy policy 3.2 names the one thing that is not end-to-end encrypted: the tastes a family plans around.

item.title: Canada now has a Children's Privacy Code. Here is what Linnea does with a child's health data.
item.description: The Privacy Commissioner of Canada launched a Children's Privacy Code on 20 October. We read it against how Linnea handles a child's profile kept by a parent.

item.title: Your health app has service providers. The OPC just published how to assess them.
item.description: Canada's Privacy Commissioner has published guidance on assessing third-party service providers. We read Linnea's privacy policy against it, section by section.

item.title: Readiness scores are here. A health record's job is to stay legible.
item.description: Apple's new watches sample heart rate every five seconds. More signal raises the bar for a personal health record: aggregate on device, explain every score, claim less.
